```{r}
#| label: setup

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EXAMPLE DASHBOARD for CDAE 7990. Every number on every page is computed in
# this file, so you can read top to bottom and see where each one comes from.
#
# Packages: everything here is in your Posit Cloud workspace except reactable
# (the searchable table on the last page). Install it once with
#   install.packages("reactable")
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(ggspatial)
library(mapgl)
library(reactable)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# One theme for every static figure, so the pages look like one product
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))

# Small helpers for formatting numbers in text and value boxes
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 10^-digits)
# (\u00a0 is a non-breaking space: a value box value with a plain space breaks)
pts <- function(x) paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), round(100 * x, 1), "\u00a0pts")

# One color per idea, used on every page:
# purple = older residents, orange = nursing homes, grey = U.S. benchmark
age_purple  <- "#54278F"
home_orange <- "#B04E0A"
```

```{r}
#| label: data-census

# ---- 1. Which counties are in the NBRC region? ----------------------------
# The same 63-county list we used in Week 9 (it lives in the site's data/ folder)
nbrc_counties <- read_csv("../data/nbrc_counties_fips.csv",
                          col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

nbrc_states <- c("ME", "NH", "NY", "VT")

# ---- 2. Age data from the ACS ---------------------------------------------
# B01001 is "Sex by Age." Lines 020-025 are men 65+, lines 044-049 are women 65+.
age_vars <- c(total = "B01001_001",
              sprintf("B01001_%03d", c(20:25, 44:49)))

# Add up the twelve 65+ lines into one count, then take the share
sum_65_plus <- function(acs_df) {
  acs_df |>
    group_by(GEOID, NAME) |>
    summarize(pop   = sum(estimate[variable == "total"]),
              pop65 = sum(estimate[variable != "total"]),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(share65 = pop65 / pop)
}

# Counties, 2020-2024 ACS, with geometry for the maps
county_age_2024 <- get_acs(geography = "county", state = nbrc_states,
                           variables = age_vars, year = 2024,
                           survey = "acs5") |>
  sum_65_plus() |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips)

# Counties, 2015-2019 ACS: the "before" picture for the change page
county_age_2019 <- get_acs(geography = "county", state = nbrc_states,
                           variables = age_vars, year = 2019,
                           survey = "acs5") |>
  sum_65_plus() |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips)

# The whole country, both years, as a benchmark
us_age_2024 <- get_acs(geography = "us", variables = age_vars,
                       year = 2024, survey = "acs5") |> sum_65_plus()
us_age_2019 <- get_acs(geography = "us", variables = age_vars,
                       year = 2019, survey = "acs5") |> sum_65_plus()

# One row per county with both years side by side
county_change <- county_age_2024 |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, pop, pop65, share65) |>
  left_join(county_age_2019 |> select(GEOID, share65_2019 = share65),
            by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(change = share65 - share65_2019,
         county = str_remove(NAME, " County"),     # "Essex, Vermont"
         state  = str_extract(NAME, "[^,]+$") |> str_trim())

# Regional totals (sum the counts first, THEN divide; don't average shares)
nbrc_share_2024 <- sum(county_age_2024$pop65) / sum(county_age_2024$pop)
nbrc_share_2019 <- sum(county_age_2019$pop65) / sum(county_age_2019$pop)
us_share_2024   <- us_age_2024$share65
us_share_2019   <- us_age_2019$share65

n_above_us <- sum(county_change$share65 > us_share_2024)

# County shapes from TIGER (cartographic boundary files, cb = TRUE)
county_shapes <- counties(state = nbrc_states, cb = TRUE, year = 2024,
                          progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips) |>
  select(GEOID)
```

```{r}
#| label: data-nursing-homes

# ---- 3. Nursing homes from CMS --------------------------------------------
# CMS "Provider Information" file: one row per Medicare/Medicaid-certified
# nursing home in the country, with coordinates, beds, and star ratings.
# https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/4pq5-n9py
# The download link changes every month, so we saved a dated copy.
homes_raw <- read_csv("data/NH_ProviderInfo_Oct2026.csv",
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

# Keep the columns we use and give them short names
homes_us <- homes_raw |>
  filter(State %in% c(state.abb, "DC")) |>          # 50 states + DC
  transmute(name      = str_to_title(`Provider Name`),
            town      = str_to_title(`City/Town`),
            state     = State,
            beds      = `Number of Certified Beds`,
            residents = `Average Number of Residents per Day`,
            stars     = `Overall Rating`,
            ownership = `Ownership Type`,
            turnover  = `Total nursing staff turnover`,
            staff_hrs = `Reported Total Nurse Staffing Hours per Resident per Day`,
            lon = Longitude, lat = Latitude)

# Points: st_as_sf() turns lon/lat columns into geometry (as in HW4)
homes_sf <- homes_us |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(county_shapes))

# Spatial join: which NBRC county does each home sit in?
# left = FALSE drops every home outside the region.
nbrc_homes <- homes_sf |>
  st_join(county_shapes, left = FALSE)

# Beds per county, then per 1,000 residents 65+
county_beds <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarize(homes = n(), beds = sum(beds, na.rm = TRUE))

county_stats <- county_change |>
  left_join(county_beds, by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(homes = replace_na(homes, 0),
         beds  = replace_na(beds, 0),
         beds_per_1k = beds / pop65 * 1000)

# Regional and national benchmarks
nbrc_beds_per_1k <- sum(county_stats$beds) / sum(county_stats$pop65) * 1000
us_beds_per_1k   <- sum(homes_us$beds, na.rm = TRUE) / us_age_2024$pop65 * 1000

no_home_counties <- county_stats |> filter(homes == 0)

nbrc_turnover <- median(nbrc_homes$turnover, na.rm = TRUE)
us_turnover   <- median(homes_us$turnover, na.rm = TRUE)
nbrc_staff    <- median(nbrc_homes$staff_hrs, na.rm = TRUE)
us_staff      <- median(homes_us$staff_hrs, na.rm = TRUE)

# Share of rated homes with one star
one_star <- function(x) mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
nbrc_one_star <- one_star(nbrc_homes$stars)
us_one_star   <- one_star(homes_us$stars)

# Do older counties have fewer beds per senior?
age_beds_cor <- cor(county_stats$share65, county_stats$beds_per_1k)

# The map layers need everything in one sf object per layer
county_map <- county_shapes |>
  left_join(county_stats, by = "GEOID")
```

### Column {width="70%"}

```{r}
#| label: map-overview
#| title: "Share of residents 65+ by county, with nursing homes (circle area = beds)"

# Popups: one HTML string per feature, shown when you click it
county_map <- county_map |>
  mutate(
    hover = county,
    popup = glue::glue(
      "<strong>{county}</strong><br>",
      "Residents 65+: {pct(share65)}<br>",
      "Nursing homes: {homes}<br>",
      "Beds per 1,000 residents 65+: {round(beds_per_1k, 1)}"
    )
  )

# Circle AREA should track beds, so the radius grows with the square root
home_points <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(
    radius = sqrt(beds) * 0.9,
    star_text = if_else(is.na(stars), "not rated",
                        paste0(stars, " of 5 stars")),
    hover = name,
    popup = glue::glue(
      "<strong>{name}</strong><br>{town}, {state}<br>",
      "Certified beds: {beds}<br>",
      "CMS rating: {star_text}<br>",
      "Nursing staff turnover: {ifelse(is.na(turnover), 'n/a', paste0(turnover, '%'))}"
    )
  )

purples <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(5, "Purples")
share_breaks <- c(0.15, 0.19, 0.23, 0.27, 0.31)

legend_beds <- c(50, 150, 300)

maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"),
         bounds = st_transform(county_map, 4326)) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "Counties",
    source = st_transform(county_map, 4326),
    fill_color = interpolate(column = "share65",
                             values = share_breaks,
                             stops = purples),
    fill_opacity = 0.75,
    fill_outline_color = "white",
    tooltip = "hover",
    popup = "popup"
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id = "Nursing homes",
    source = home_points,
    circle_color = home_orange,
    circle_radius = get_column("radius"),
    circle_opacity = 0.8,
    circle_stroke_color = "white",
    circle_stroke_width = 1,
    tooltip = "hover",
    popup = "popup"
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Residents 65+",
    values = pct(share_breaks, 0),
    colors = purples,
    type = "continuous",
    position = "bottom-left",
    width = "250px"
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Certified beds",
    values = legend_beds,
    colors = rep(home_orange, 3),
    sizes = 2 * sqrt(legend_beds) * 0.9,
    type = "categorical",
    circular_patches = TRUE,
    position = "bottom-right",
    margin_bottom = 30,
    add = TRUE
  ) |>
  add_layers_control(position = "top-right", collapsible = FALSE) |>
  add_navigation_control(position = "top-left") |>
  add_fullscreen_control(position = "top-left")
```

### Column {width="30%"}

::: {.card .bottom-line title="Bottom line"}
**The Northern Border region is older than the country and getting older faster. The oldest counties tend to have the fewest nursing home beds per senior.**

**Older.** `{r} pct(nbrc_share_2024)` of the region's residents are 65 or older, compared with `{r} pct(us_share_2024)` nationally. `{r} n_above_us` of the 63 NBRC counties are above the national share.

**Aging faster.** Since 2015–2019, the region's 65+ share rose `{r} round(100 * (nbrc_share_2024 - nbrc_share_2019), 1)` points, against `{r} round(100 * (us_share_2024 - us_share_2019), 1)` points for the U.S.

**Care is thinnest where need is highest.** Counties with a larger 65+ share have fewer nursing home beds per 1,000 seniors (correlation of `{r} round(age_beds_cor, 2)`). `{r} nrow(no_home_counties)` counties have no certified nursing home at all.

**How to use this map.** Hover over a county or a circle for its name and click for details. Use the box in the top right to turn the nursing homes off.
:::

change_map <- ggplot(county_map) +

  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Purples", direction = 1,
                       labels = \(x) paste0("+", round(100 * x, 1)),

  annotation_scale(location = "br", width_hint = 0.25) +
  labs(caption = "Source: ACS 5-year estimates, 2015–2019 and 2020–2024, table B01001") +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +

        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))

change_map

```{r}
#| label: dumbbell
#| title: "The 15 oldest counties, then and now"

oldest_15 <- county_change |>
  slice_max(share65, n = 15) |>
  mutate(county = fct_reorder(county, share65))

dumbbell <- ggplot(oldest_15) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = us_share_2024, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = us_share_2024, y = levels(oldest_15$county)[15],
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = 0.5,
           label = paste0("U.S., 2020–24: ", pct(us_share_2024)),
           color = "grey40", size = 3.8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = share65_2019, xend = share65, y = county, yend = county),
               color = "grey70", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = share65_2019, y = county, color = "2015–2019"), size = 3.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = share65, y = county, color = "2020–2024"), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2015–2019" = "grey60", "2020–2024" = age_purple),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0.15, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Share of residents 65+", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

dumbbell
```

```{r}
#| label: scatter
#| title: "Older counties have fewer nursing home beds per senior"

# Label a handful of counties so readers can find their bearings:
# the oldest, the youngest, the most beds per senior, and the largest
# county with no nursing home. hjust keeps edge labels inside the panel.
label_these <- county_stats |>
  filter(share65 == max(share65) | beds_per_1k == max(beds_per_1k) |
           share65 == min(share65) |
           (homes == 0 & pop65 == max(pop65[homes == 0]))) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(str_remove(county, ",.*"), ", ",
                        state.abb[match(state, state.name)]),
         hjust = case_when(share65 == max(county_stats$share65) ~ 1,
                           share65 == min(county_stats$share65) ~ 0,
                           .default = 0.5))

beds_scatter <- ggplot(county_stats, aes(x = share65, y = beds_per_1k)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nbrc_beds_per_1k, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.335, y = nbrc_beds_per_1k, vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1,
           label = "NBRC region overall", color = "grey40", size = 3.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = pop65), color = age_purple, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = label_these, aes(label = label, hjust = hjust),
            vjust = -1.2, size = 3.6, color = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, labels = scales::label_comma(),
                  name = "Residents 65+") +
  labs(x = "Share of residents 65+ (2020–2024)",
       y = "Certified beds per 1,000 residents 65+",
       caption = "Each circle is one NBRC county. Grey line: linear trend.") +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))

beds_scatter
```

```{r}
#| label: stars
#| title: "NBRC nursing homes skew toward lower CMS star ratings"

star_shares <- bind_rows(
  nbrc_homes |> st_drop_geometry() |> mutate(group = "NBRC region"),
  homes_us |> mutate(group = "United States")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(stars)) |>
  count(group, stars) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

star_bars <- ggplot(star_shares,
                    aes(x = factor(stars), y = share, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share, 0)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NBRC region" = home_orange,
                               "United States" = "grey65"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "CMS overall rating (stars)", y = "Share of rated homes",
       caption = "Source: CMS Nursing Home Provider Information, October 2026") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))

star_bars
```

# Data & Methods

## Row

### Column {width="65%"}

```{r}
#| label: table
#| title: !expr paste("All", nrow(nbrc_homes), "certified nursing homes in NBRC counties (search, sort, or filter)")

home_table <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(stars = if_else(is.na(stars), "not rated",
                         strrep("★", stars))) |>
  select(Name = name, Town = town, State = state, Beds = beds,
         `Avg. residents` = residents, Rating = stars,
         `Staff turnover (%)` = turnover, Ownership = ownership) |>
  arrange(State, Town)

reactable(home_table,
          searchable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, striped = TRUE,
          highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 15,
          columns = list(
            Name = colDef(minWidth = 200),
            `Avg. residents` = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 0)),
            Ownership = colDef(minWidth = 160)
          ))
```

### Column {width="35%"}

::: {.card title="Sources and methods"}
**Population.** American Community Survey 5-year estimates (2015–2019 and 2020–2024), table B01001 (Sex by Age), pulled with `tidycensus`. "65+" adds up the twelve age-and-sex lines for 65 and older. Regional shares add up counts across counties first and then divide, rather than averaging county percentages.

**Nursing homes.** CMS Nursing Home Provider Information, October 2026 release. It covers Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing homes only, so assisted living and residential care are not in these counts. Each home was placed in a county with a spatial join (`st_join()`) on its CMS coordinates. One Amsterdam, NY home that CMS lists in Montgomery County falls just inside Fulton County this way; both are NBRC counties.

**Region.** The 63 NBRC counties in Maine, New Hampshire, New York, and Vermont. County shapes are 2024 Census cartographic boundary files (`tigris`, `cb = TRUE`).

**Caveats.** ACS figures are estimates with margins of error, which are widest for the smallest counties (Hamilton County, NY has fewer than 2,000 residents 65+). Beds per 1,000 seniors ignores people crossing county lines for care, so a county with no home may be served by a neighbor.

**Code.** Every number in this dashboard is computed in its source file. Use the GitHub button in the top right to read it.
:::
